title: Aligned Delegates currently serve as the primary Ecosystem Spell Validators
content:
A.1.10.2.4.12.1.1 states that Ecosystem Spell Validators "are members of the Sky Ecosystem responsible for performing the Spell validation process. **Currently, Aligned Delegates serve as the primary Spell validators** for the Sky Ecosystem."

That sentence merges two roles that are conceptually distinct. Aligned Delegates hold delegated voting power and vote on Governance Polls; Ecosystem Validators perform an adversarial technical check on deployed bytecode — running Foundry tests, decoding deployment opcodes, diffing Etherscan source against GitHub, verifying keccak hashes. The first role is judgment about policy; the second is a demanding engineering audit.

Two consequences follow. First, validation coverage depends on the technical capability of a set of people selected for governance alignment, not for smart-contract expertise — and the process compensates with unusually explicit step-by-step instructions, which reads as an attempt to make the checks executable by non-specialists.

Second, the party voting on a proposal is the party certifying that the proposal's code is honest. That is not a conflict in the ordinary sense — a delegate has no incentive to pass a malicious Spell — but it does mean the validation layer is not independent of the voting layer, so a failure of delegate diligence removes both checks at once.

The hedge "currently" signals the Atlas expects this to change. Until it does, Ecosystem Validation's strength is bounded by how many delegates actually run the checks, which nothing in this section requires them to disclose — A.1.10.2.4.12.4.1 makes public validation ideal but not mandatory.
description: A.1.10.2.4.12.1.1 places technical verification with the same parties who cast delegated votes, and the word 'currently' marks the arrangement as provisional rather than designed.
